conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up the coding agent with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Downloaded the 8 DECODE images and the attached key document with the session cookie.
Read the pages: a clear English despatch of Lee and Poyntz to Wolsey; cipher only in three runs on f. 184v.
Transcribed the contemporary interlinear decipherment of the three runs.
Spot-checked one run against Tomokiyo's Lee-Worcester key: sigma tau c c bottom = c a n n o under 'can not'.

R8565: searched the Letters and Papers calendar for 17 July 1527 (British History Online, vol. IV pp. 1478-1490); nos. 3270-3272 are the Lee, Ghinucci and Poyntz despatches of that day, 3271 noted 'The cipher deciphered by Tuke ... One part of this despatch is separated from the other', its second part at f. 166.
R8565: full DECODE images refused without login (no cookie on this machine); the eight public thumbnails downloaded.

R8565: placed by foliation. R8566 (new ff. 178-181, old 170-173) is L&P 3270 at f. 170, so new ff. 174-177 = old 166-169 = the separated part of L&P 3271; the thumbnails show a clear English despatch with interlinear bands, three signatures and an address leaf.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R8567's interlinear decipherment (plaintext.txt); for R8565 nothing is in the folder: L&P IV 3271's deciphered passages (print, 1872) and the interlinear bands on the images are not copied, and neither record's cipher was transcribed (project work)

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): R8567's plaintext.txt reads; R8565 has no text in the repository (calendar paraphrases only). R8565 relabelled decoded, not read, with an excerpt note pointing to the DECODE images and L&P IV 3271, both reachable; class already solved kept; fraction_read 1 -> about 0.38 (estimated by runs).

R8565 DECODE record fetched logged in (b31_fetch.py): 8 full-resolution images and Tomokiyo's key png; every image opened. P1 confirms the record is the separated second part of L&P IV 3271 ('the xv of Julie ... Mons. de Pratt and Mons. de Burlans'). Cipher in five places (ff. 174r one word, 174v-175r, 175r, 176v, 177r), each with a contemporary decipherment over or between the lines or in the margin; ff. 175v-176r clear. The decipherment transcribed from 2-3x crops (b31_crop.py).

R8565: each decipherment passage checked against the cipher signs with Tomokiyo's Lee-Worcester key (and, frenchemen, had not been, browght hym, madrill, his, ever you have ben, raison, amite, shal we have that he shal not rendre, handes, frendes that knowes non so great, this like you, than to this man that is nothing mete for it, de tarbes now shewed, fourth instruction, kept it, oon devise, than of any other prince): every checked word agrees; sign 5 = 'not' at two places (not in the table, flagged for review). L&P IV 3271 (archive.org OCR) agrees with the content.

R8565 reading scored: 0.909 (20/22) explicit-hole share, 0.227 plain (1527 spelling); sentences hold; look-alike letters 0. R8565 decoded, not read -> read (grade B); fraction_read 0.38 -> 1 (by runs).

outcome.method_basis: R8567's three cipher runs carry an interlinear decipherment on f. 184v and R8565 was deciphered by Tuke, calendared in L&P IV 3271; Tomokiyo's key on DECODE R8566 was only spot-checked against them.
outcome.notes: Both records read at the time: R8567 from its interlinear decipherment, R8565 from Tuke's decipherment in print (L&P IV 3271) and on the page. Nothing new to read. R8565 identified from the thumbnails and the calendar; the full images were not viewed. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R8565 decoded, not read (no text of it in the repository); class already solved kept (Tuke's decipherment, in print); fraction_read 1 -> about 0.38.

texts.label: R8567, Vesp. C IV ff. 182-185, Valladolid, July 1527 (contemporary interlinear decipherment of the three runs on f. 184v)
texts.summary: A long clear English despatch of Edward Lee and Sir Francis Poyntz to Wolsey on their audiences with Charles V and Gattinara (Francesco Sforza, the two millions of the ransom, the treaty of Madrid); three short runs in the Lee-Worcester cipher are deciphered above the line: 'we know well you will kepe hit full well secrets from the frenchemen'.

texts.label: R8565, Vesp. C IV ff. 174-177, Valladolid, 17 July 1527 (L&P IV 3271, Tuke's decipherment in italics)
texts.summary: Part of the joint despatch of Ghinucci, Lee and Poyntz to Wolsey, 17 July 1527, calendared in full in Letters and Papers Henry VIII IV no. 3271: the French envoy's dealings, the suggestion that the Emperor might give the duchy of Milan with the daughter of Portugal to the Duke of Richmond, and the bishop of Tarbes's fourth instruction. The interlinear decipherment is only on the DECODE images.

reading_review.note: texts/R8565_reading.md follows the contemporary decipherment (Tuke's, per L&P IV 3271) written over and between the cipher lines of ff. 174v, 175r, 176v, 177r, read on the full-resolution DECODE images (first viewed 23 Oct 2026); each passage checked against the signs with Tomokiyo's Lee-Worcester key, every checked word agrees. Reading body 0.909 (20/22) counting explicit holes only, 0.227 plain (1527 spelling). Look-alike letters 0. Open: [?bere] (f. 174v) and four words written over each other on f. 176v before 'the doughter of Portugalo' (illegible at this resolution).

outcome.fraction_read_source: Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (batch b31): both documents read. R8567's three runs (plaintext.txt) and R8565's five cipher passages (texts/R8565_reading.md, from the contemporary decipherment checked against the signs) = all cipher runs of the two records; no token count of the cipher exists, so by runs: 8 of 8.
